title: NanoClaw adds an opt-in hardened runtime for open-source agents
friendlyTitle: NanoClaw makes the software inside its agent sandbox safer
summary: NanoClaw and Echo have released a free, opt-in runtime that rebuilds and patches the browser, libraries and command-line tools inside an agent sandbox. The companies say this cuts known vulnerabilities from thousands to near zero while retaining a locally built, unauthenticated alternative.
friendlySummary: A new optional runtime removes unnecessary software and patches the browser and tools used by NanoClaw agents. The normal local setup is still available.
whyItMatters: A sandbox limits damage but does not fix vulnerable software inside it. People operating agents that browse untrusted pages or open files should treat the runtime like an employee laptop: minimise components, patch continuously and keep credentials behind policy controls.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Agent sandboxes also need updates and security fixes. This can reduce known weak points, but users should still limit access and protect credentials.
